coverage.main: Read all nineteen pages of arXiv 2402.14016v2 (4 July 2024): Sections 1-9, Algorithm 1, Tables 1-4, Figures 1-4 and Appendices A-I (phrases Table 5, asymmetric ablations Tables 6-7, comparative transfer Figure 5, direct Llama2 attack Figure 6, GCG Table 8, per-candidate Tables 9-32, prompts Figures 7-8). The nineteen-page EMNLP 2024 version of record (pp. 7499-7517) was also retrieved; all 1,638 decimal values match those in arXiv v2.
coverage.supplement: Appendices A-I are embedded in both versions and read.
coverage.excluded_results: Figure 2, Table 3, Tables 6-14, 21-22 and Appendix D Figure 6 are direct attacks on the attacked judge (FlanT5-xl or Llama2-7B). Tables 29-32 (Appendix H) are direct attacks on UniEval. Tables 1-2 report clean assessment correlation. Table 4 and Figure 4 evaluate perplexity detection. Table 8 compares GCG with greedy search on the surrogate.

result_groups.population: Test split (80% of contexts) of SummEval (16 candidates per context) and TopicalChat (6 per context); universal phrases of 1-4 words learned by greedy search on FlanT5-xl using 2 candidates of the 20% development split; transferred to GPT3.5, Mistral-7B and Llama2-7B absolute scorers
result_groups.outcome: average rank of the attacked candidate among unattacked candidates (Eq. 8), and average predicted score
result_groups.evidence: Every test candidate is attacked and ranked (Eq. 8 averages over all contexts and candidates), and per-candidate unattacked scores are printed. However, rank or score inflation has no per-item clean-correct or source-success event, so neither field maps onto this outcome.

result_groups.population: Same test splits; comparative-assessment phrases learned on FlanT5-xl and transferred to Llama2-7B and Mistral-7B comparative judges
result_groups.outcome: average rank of the attacked candidate (graphical)

f1.evidence: Clean assessment quality (Spearman correlation) and unattacked per-candidate scores and ranks are reported, which is positive baseline evidence. A clean classification accuracy is not defined for a score-inflation outcome.

f2.evidence: No clean-correct event exists for either scope.

f3.evidence: All test candidates are attacked and averaged, but source success is not defined per item for a universal phrase.

f4.evidence: Average ranks and scores are continuous. Candidate and context counts follow from the dataset description, but no counted events are reported.

f5.evidence: The perturbation is a concatenated phrase of L <= 4 vocabulary words (budget in words); an L-infinity or L2 radius does not apply to discrete text. Reported in the non-image stratum, as for rank 1.

f6.evidence: The official repository releases greedy/GCG attack, evaluation and model wrappers for FlanT5, Llama, OpenAI and UniEval, and Appendix A prints every learned phrase. The GPT-3.5 target is a hosted model whose 2024 behaviour cannot be verified. Not executed.

artifact_checks.result: Linked in the paper. Listed via the GitHub API (29 files, head 4 July 2024): train_attack.py, attack.py, evaluate.py, src/attacker/greedy.py and gcg.py, src/models/flant5.py, llama.py, openai.py and unieval.py, src/data/load_data.py. Not executed.

bounds_checks.reason: Rank or score inflation of an LLM judge is not a misclassification probability.

limitations: Non-blind evidence audit. Fields 1-4 are unclear because of outcome mapping, not deficient reporting.
